title: 4 Days in Jackson Hole, Wyoming: Peaks, Wildlife & Western Flavor
description: Your personalized Jackson Hole itinerary with hiking, rafting, wildlife, hot springs, and the best restaurants.

days.title: Arrive & Explore Jackson Town Square
days.description: Fly into Jackson Hole Airport (JAC), grab your rental, settle into your lodging, and spend the afternoon exploring the charming western town of Jackson. Ease in with good food and iconic elk-antler arches.

activities.name: Airport to Town & Get Oriented
activities.description: Jackson Hole Airport is just 15 minutes from downtown Jackson — one of the most scenic airport approaches in the country with the Tetons rising right outside your window. Pick up your rental and head to your lodging. For groups of 5+, an Airbnb in town or a condo in Teton Village is the best value. Drop your bags, then walk to the iconic Town Square with its four elk-antler arches. Browse the galleries and western shops along the boardwalks.

activities.name: Dinner at Handfire Pizza + Million Dollar Cowboy Bar
activities.description: For your first night, keep it fun and group-friendly. Handfire Pizza is a wood-fired pizza joint in the heart of Jackson — perfect for sharing pies with a big group. After dinner, walk next door to the legendary Million Dollar Cowboy Bar on the town square. The barstools are actual saddles, there's live country music most nights, and two-stepping on the dance floor is basically required. It's touristy, it's fun, and it's the essential Jackson Hole first-night experience.

days.neighborhoods: Grand Teton National Park · Snake River
days.title: Grand Teton National Park & Snake River Rafting
days.description: Your biggest adventure day — morning in Grand Teton National Park with one of the most scenic drives in America, followed by afternoon whitewater rafting through the Snake River Canyon. This is the day you'll remember forever.

activities.time: 🌅 Morning — Grand Teton Scenic Drive & Hike
activities.name: Teton Park Road & Taggart Lake Trail
activities.description: Start early (7am) and drive the Teton Park Road — the views of the Cathedral Group (Grand Teton, Mt. Owen, Teewinot) reflected in the Snake River are jaw-dropping. Stop at Schwabacher Landing for the iconic reflection shot, then hike the Taggart Lake Trail — a moderate 3.2-mile round trip through wildflower meadows to a stunning glacial lake at the base of the Tetons. Perfect for a group, and the late-August wildflowers are still going strong.

activities.name: Snake River Canyon — Class II–III Rapids
activities.description: Book a whitewater rafting trip through Snake River Canyon with Dave Hansen Whitewater or Barker-Ewing. The 8-mile canyon run features Class II–III rapids with names like "Big Kahuna," "Lunch Counter," and "Rope." It's thrilling without being terrifying — perfect for a group with mixed comfort levels. August water levels are ideal. You'll be splashing through stunning canyon walls with bald eagles overhead.

activities.name: Craft Beers & Burgers at Bin22
activities.description: After a massive adventure day, you've earned it. Bin22 is a wine bar and bistro with an excellent small-plates menu — think elevated comfort food. The charcuterie boards are perfect for sharing with a group. If the crew wants something more casual, walk to Snake River Brewing — Wyoming's first and most-awarded craft brewery. Their Pako's Dream Pilsner and Zonker Stout are iconic.

days.title: Teton Village, Via Ferrata & Relaxation
days.description: Split the group today — adrenaline seekers tackle the via ferrata climbing route at the resort, while the relaxation crew soaks in hot springs and explores galleries. Reunite for the best meal of the trip.

activities.name: Jackson Hole Mountain Resort
activities.description: Adventure option: Ride the iconic Aerial Tram to the summit of Rendezvous Mountain (10,450 feet). The views from the top are staggering — you can see into three states and Yellowstone. For the brave, book the Via Ferrata climbing route ($185/person, guide included) — a fixed-rope mountain climbing experience along exposed ridges with stunning drops. No climbing experience needed, just nerves and a head for heights. Chill option: Skip the via ferrata and just ride the tram up ($45) — hike the Wildflower Trail at the top or simply enjoy waffles at Corbet's Cabin, the highest restaurant in Wyoming, accessible only by tram.

activities.name: Astoria Hot Springs or Granite Hot Springs
activities.description: Astoria Hot Springs (20 min south of Jackson) is the easy, accessible option — a beautifully restored natural hot spring pool right on the Snake River. Soak in 104°F mineral water with mountain views. Affordable ($15/adult) and great for groups. Granite Hot Springs (35 min south, then a scenic gravel road) is more remote and rugged — a natural pool in the Gros Ventre Range fed by a 112°F spring. The drive through the Hoback Canyon is beautiful. In August, the pool is cooled to ~93°F — refreshing rather than scalding.

activities.name: The Best Meal of Your Trip
activities.description: Tonight is your group's splurge dinner. Gather is the restaurant everyone in Jackson raves about — seasonal, farm-to-table, with a constantly evolving menu featuring local elk, bison, trout, and foraged ingredients. The tasting menu is incredible but à la carte works too. For a more casual-but-still-amazing alternative, Glorietta serves stunning Italian-meets-mountain cuisine in a gorgeous space.

days.title: Wildlife Safari & Western Cookout
days.description: Late August is prime wildlife season. Start with a guided wildlife safari at dawn, spend the afternoon on an easy hike, and cap the trip with a classic western chuck-wagon cookout under the stars.

activities.name: Guided Wildlife Tour at Dawn
activities.description: Book a sunrise wildlife safari with EcoTour Adventures or BrushBuck Wildlife Tours. The guides use spotting scopes and know exactly where the animals are. Late August, you'll likely see moose in the willow flats, elk herds gathering for fall migration, bison, pronghorn, bald eagles, and — if you're lucky — grizzly bears or wolves at a distance. The light at dawn in the Tetons is photographer's paradise.

activities.name: Easy Hike & Last-Minute Shopping
activities.description: Take a chill afternoon hike on the Cache Creek Trail — it starts right from the edge of downtown Jackson (yes, you can walk to the trailhead). A flat, shaded 3-mile out-and-back along the creek through aspens. Perfect for sore legs after a big trip. After, browse the Jackson galleries and shops on the town square. The Teton Toy Store and Made are great for unique souvenirs.

activities.name: Bar T5 Covered Wagon Ride & Cookout
activities.description: The perfect final night. Bar T5 takes your group on a horse-drawn covered wagon ride into Cache Creek Canyon, where they serve a full western cookout dinner — steak, roasted chicken, cornbread, baked beans, Dutch oven cobbler. There's live cowboy music, a campfire, and Teton views. It's hokey in the best possible way and genuinely fun for a group. Book in advance — this is one of the most popular activities in Jackson.

days.title: Sunrise at the Tetons & Farewell
days.description: Your last morning — catch one final sunrise over the Teton Range, grab a legendary breakfast, and head to the airport with a head full of mountain memories.

activities.name: The Most Iconic View in Wyoming
activities.description: Set your alarm for 5:45am and drive 25 minutes north to Oxbow Bend on the Snake River. This is the postcard shot — Mt. Moran reflected perfectly in the still morning water, often with mist rising off the surface and a moose wading through. Late August sunrise is around 6:45am. Get there 20 minutes early, set up, and watch the Tetons light up gold and pink. The whole group will be speechless.

activities.name: Head to JAC Airport
activities.description: Jackson Hole Airport is tiny and inside Grand Teton National Park — which means even your departure is scenic. It's only 15 minutes from town, but allow extra time in August (busy season). Take one last look at the Tetons from the terminal and start planning your winter return trip for skiing.

editorialSummary: Your personalized Jackson Hole itinerary with hiking, rafting, wildlife, hot springs, and the best restaurants.
